import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between petal length and petal width,
# with species differentiated by color. Petal dimensions often show the clearest separation.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=100,  # size of the markers
    alpha=0.8, # transparency
    palette='viridis' # color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species (Iris Dataset)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement
plt.legend(title='Species', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between petal length and petal width,
# with species differentiated by color. Petal dimensions often show the clearest separation.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species',
    s=100,  # size of the markers
    alpha=0.8, # transparency
    palette='viridis' # color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species (Iris Dataset)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement
